quote_found: Results: 'The incidence of moderate or severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome was significantly lower in the frozen-embryo group than in the fresh-embryo group (1.3% vs. 7.1%), for a rate ratio of 0.19 (95% CI, 0.10 to 0.37; P<0.001) (Table 4).' Methods: 'On the day of oocyte retrieval, if an adequate number of oocytes (>3 and <30) were retrieved and the patient was at low risk for the ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (as determined by local investigators), patients were randomly assigned to one of the two study groups in a 1:1 ratio, stratified according to study site.'
what_is_wrong: The effect estimate, the outcome definition and the quote are all EXACT - 'moderate or severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome' is genuinely the trial's wording, it is genuinely a prespecified secondary outcome, and 'Moderate and severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndromes were defined according to accepted criteria' with reference 25 = Golan et al. 1989 is genuinely in the Methods. What is WRONG is the claim's field high_risk_excluded: 'no - this trial deliberately enrolled PCOS women, the archetypal high-OHSS-risk population, which is why the fresh-arm OHSS rate is high (7.1%)'. Chen 2016 DID exclude high-OHSS-risk women, at exactly the same point and by exactly the same mechanism as Shi 2018: randomisation happened on the day of oocyte retrieval and only patients 'at low risk for the ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (as determined by local investigators)' (and with >3 and <30 oocytes) were randomised. The claim's causal gloss is therefore unsupported: the 7.1% fresh-arm rate arose DESPITE screening out high-risk women, not because they were included. This also silently undermines the contrast the claim set drew in SQ2-C3's notes, which presents Shi 2018 as the trial that uniquely 'screened out' high-risk women.

quote_found: Table II, verbatim row and footnote: 'Maternal safety: ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome | 11 (3.6%) | 25 (8.1%) | 0.44 (0.18 to 1.10) | 0.44 (0.15 to 1.30) | 0.051' under column heads 'Unadjusted risk ratio (95 or 99% CI) | Adjusted* risk ratio (95 or 99% CI) | P-value', with the table footnote: 'Data are presented as n (%), n/N (%), or n. CIs are 95% for the primary outcome and 99% for all secondary outcomes. P-values are for adjusted estimates when available, or unadjusted estimates otherwise.'
what_is_wrong: The headline is exact - 'The risk of OHSS was 3.6% (11/307) in the elective freeze arm compared to 8.1% (25/309) in the fresh embryo transfer arm (RR 0.44, 99% CI: 0.15 to 1.30) (Table II). The severity of ovarian hyperstimulation was only mild to moderate in the elective freeze group, whereas there were 6 cases (1.9%) of severe OHSS in the fresh embryo transfer group' is verbatim, 619 couples across 18 UK clinics 2016-2019 is verbatim, single embryo transfer 249/298 (83.6%) and 247/303 (81.5%) confirms 'over 80%', the exclusion 'a clinical indication for an elective freeze such as OHSS or fertility preservation' is verbatim, and 'The risk of OHSS was not reduced by an elective freeze policy' is verbatim. WHAT IS WRONG is the claim's statistical annotation: 'the corresponding 95% CI given in the outcome table is 0.18 to 1.10'. It is not a 95% CI. Table II's own footnote states 'CIs are 95% for the primary outcome and 99% for all secondary outcomes', and OHSS is a secondary outcome, so 0.44 (0.18 to 1.10) is the UNADJUSTED RR with a 99% CI while 0.44 (0.15 to 1.30) is the ADJUSTED RR with a 99% CI - the claim has both mislabelled the interval level and conflated unadjusted with adjusted. I verified this arithmetically: for 11/307 vs 25/309, log-RR SE = 0.353, giving a 99% CI of 0.18 to 1.10 (matching the table exactly) and a 95% CI of 0.22 to 0.88. This is material, not cosmetic: the true 95% interval EXCLUDES 1, so the trial's 'non-significant' verdict rests entirely on its prespecified 99% intervals, and a reader relying on the claim's annotation would report a non-significant 95% CI that does not exist. The claim set is internally inconsistent on this point - SQ2-C14's notes correctly label the same column's preterm-delivery entry (0.91, 0.31 to 2.65) as a 99% CI.

what_is_wrong: OUTCOME DEFINITION MISQUOTED. The claim's outcome_definition field states the review prespecified HDP as 'Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, comprising pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH), pre-eclampsia (PE) and [eclampsia]'. The review's Methods actually read '...pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH), pre-eclampsia (PE) and haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets in the blood (HELLP syndrome)'. The bracketed '[eclampsia]' is a reconstruction presented inside quotation marks as the review's own wording, and it is wrong: the third component of the composite is HELLP syndrome, not eclampsia. Everything else in this claim survived attack and is EXACT: 63/1962 vs 29/1978, Peto OR 2.15 [1.42, 3.25], Chi2 = 2.84, df = 2 (P = 0.24), I2 = 29%, Z = 3.63 (P = 0.0003); the denominators really are per randomised woman (746/762, 391/391, 825/825); the overall-across-subgroups figures the claim reports (1.80 [1.23, 2.64], I2 = 59%, subgroup difference Chi2 = 4.46, df = 1, P = 0.03, I2 = 77.6%) are exact; the Summary of Findings row '15 per 1000 ... 31 per 1000 (21 to 46)' is exact; and Vuong 2018 does sit left of the null in both subgroups. quote_found: NEJM Results, verbatim: 'However, the incidence of preeclampsia was significantly higher with frozen-embryo transfer (4.4% vs. 1.4%), for a rate ratio of 3.12 (95% CI, 1.26 to 7.73; P=0.009), although no patient in either group had severe preeclampsia.' NEJM Methods, verbatim: 'On the day of oocyte retrieval, if an adequate number of oocytes (>3 and <30) were retrieved and the patient was at low risk for the ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (as determined by local investigators), patients were randomly assigned to one of the two study groups in a 1:1 ratio...'
what_is_wrong: The quoted sentence, the percentages, the rate ratio, the CI, the P value and the 'no patient in either group had severe preeclampsia' rider are all EXACT. The defect is the same false eligibility statement as SQ2-C2: the field high_risk_excluded is set to 'no', but Chen 2016 randomised only women 'at low risk for the ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (as determined by local investigators)' on the day of oocyte retrieval. SECOND, WEAKER POINT, recorded for the caller's benefit rather than as a refutation: the claim assigns timing 'per-pregnancy' but no openly retrievable source states the Table 4 denominator - NEJM Table 4 does not render through any route I could reach (curl 403, the Unpaywall-listed PDF endpoint 403, and two parallel-cli extracts returned the body text but not the table). I can prove only that it is NOT per randomised woman: Cochrane Analysis 1.9, which I read directly, enters this trial's hypertensive disorders of pregnancy as 29/746 vs 11/762, and since pre-eclampsia is a subset of HDP a 4.4% pre-eclampsia rate cannot sit on a denominator of 746 (that would require about 33 events, more than the 29 HDP events). So the denominator is restricted to pregnancies or deliveries, consistent with but not proof of the claim's label. By analogy the sister trial Shi 2018, same investigators and journal, labels its equivalent row 'Preeclampsia among clinical pregnancies'.

Frozen single blastocyst transfer was associated with a higher risk of pre-eclampsia (16 of 512 [3.1%] vs four of 401 [1.0%]; RR 3.13, 95% CI 1.06-9.30, p=0.029).' Interpretation: '...in ovulatory women with good prognosis. The increased risk of pre-eclampsia after frozen blastocyst transfer warrants further studies.' what_is_wrong: Nothing refuted. The quote is verbatim to the character, including the split verdict (OHSS not significantly reduced, pre-eclampsia up). The OHSS outcome really is 'moderate or severe' and really is per randomised woman (825/825, corroborated on the Cochrane forest plot I read). Population 'ovulatory women with good prognosis', 1650, single blastocyst, multicentre China all exact. CAVEAT the caller should carry: the pre-eclampsia denominators 512 and 401 are never defined in any openly accessible text - the Lancet body is paywalled and there is no OA copy (Unpaywall is_oa false, no PMC record) - so the claim's 'per-pregnancy' label is an unsourced inference. What IS demonstrable is the claim's essential warning, that these are not the randomised denominators (825/825), so the pre-eclampsia RR 3.13 is on a conditional denominator while the OHSS comparison is not. Also note the CI is wide on only 20 events with a lower bound of 1.06, as the claim itself says.

retrieval_method: I downloaded the JATS full-text XML from Europe PMC MYSELF with curl and enumerated every table-wrap element and its caption with python, then parsed Table 4 and the Discussion.
quote_found: Table caption, verbatim: 'Table 4 Pregnancy outcomes and complications after the first embryo transfer (as-treated analysis). Values are number/total number (%) unless stated otherwise'. Rows: 'Maternal complications: Pregnancy induced hypertension | 2/57 (3.5) | 2/55 (3.6) | 1.00 ; Pre-eclampsia | 4/57 (7.0) | 4/55 (7.3) | 1.00'. Table 4 footnote, verbatim: 'Denominator defined as number of deliveries including stillbirths and live births, only including pregnancies and births after frozen embryo transfers in freeze-all group and fresh transfers in fresh transfer group.' For contrast, the caption of the preceding table reads: 'Table 3 Reproductive outcomes for women in freeze-all and fresh transfer groups (intention-to-treat analysis).'
what_is_wrong: PROVENANCE AND DENOMINATOR BOTH MISSTATED. (1) The claim cites 'Table 3 (maternal complications)'. Table 3 is the INTENTION-TO-TREAT reproductive-outcomes table and contains no maternal complications; the pre-eclampsia and PIH rows are in Table 4, which is explicitly labelled '(as-treated analysis)'. (2) The claim sets timing to 'per-pregnancy' and describes the population as 'pregnancies continuing beyond 22 weeks'. The table's own footnote defines the denominator as the number of DELIVERIES (stillbirths plus live births) and restricts it to 'pregnancies and births after frozen embryo transfers in freeze-all group and fresh transfers in fresh transfer group'. That is a per-delivery, as-treated denominator, not a per-pregnancy randomised comparison. This is material rather than pedantic in THIS trial specifically, because Table 2 shows 37/230 (16.1%) of the fresh arm were converted to elective frozen transfer, 24/230 (10.4%) of them for OHSS risk - those women's pregnancies came after a frozen transfer and are therefore excluded from the 55-delivery fresh-arm denominator, so the comparison labelled 'multicentre RCT' is not the randomised contrast. THE FOUR NUMBERS THEMSELVES ARE EXACT (4/57 [7.0%] vs 4/55 [7.3%], P=1.00; 2/57 [3.5%] vs 2/55 [3.6%], P=1.00), the post-hoc status of PIH is correctly stated ('Post hoc analysis was performed for selected obstetric outcomes (pregnancy induced hypertension, gestational diabetes, chorioamnionitis, postpartum haemorrhage, induction of birth, mode of birth ..., twin rates, and duration of hospital stay)' is verbatim), the pointer to 'Supplementary table S1 provides definitions of secondary outcomes' is verbatim, the Discussion passage about the corpus luteum is verbatim, and Table 2 does confirm the modified natural cycle in 160/162 (98.8%) with programmed cycle in only 2/162 (1.2%), i.e. 'all but two'.

retrieval_method: NCBI efetch db=pubmed id=36154568 returned the full structured abstract of Hypertension 2023;80(2):e6-e16 directly from NLM, independent of the publisher and of any scraper. Europe PMC core record confirms journal, volume and year and that there is no PMC full text (isOpenAccess N); Unpaywall lists only two Norwegian institutional-repository handles.
quote_found: Results, verbatim: 'Risk of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy was higher after frozen-ET compared to natural conception, both at population-level (7.4% versus 4.3%, aOR, 1.74 [95% CI, 1.61-1.89]) and within sibships (aOR, 2.02 [95% CI, 1.72-2.39]). For fresh-ET, risk was similar to natural conception, both at population-level (aOR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.07]) and within sibships (aOR, 0.99 [95% CI, 0.89-1.09]).' Methods, verbatim: 'Using the Medical Birth Registries of Denmark (1994-2014), Norway, and Sweden (1988-2015), linked to data from national quality registries and databases on assisted reproduction, we designed a population-based cohort study with within-sibship comparison. We included 4 426 691 naturally conceived, 78 300 fresh-ET, and 18 037 frozen-ET singleton pregnancies, of which 33 209 sibships were conceived using different conception methods. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) ... were estimated using multilevel logistic regression, where random effects provided conventional population-level estimates and fixed effects gave within-sibship estimates. Main models included adjustment for birth year, maternal age, parity, and country.'
what_is_wrong: Nothing refuted, and the three design-laundering traps I looked for are all avoided: the claim labels the design 'registry', labels the effect measure 'aOR' (not RR or Peto OR), and explicitly warns that the reference group is NATURAL CONCEPTION rather than fresh transfer, so the estimate is not interchangeable with the trial-based SQ2-C7. The outcome is correctly reported as hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, NOT narrowed to pre-eclampsia. Registry years, both aOR pairs, both CIs and the 7.4% versus 4.3% absolute figures are verbatim. ONE POPULATION OMISSION the caller should carry: the cohort is restricted to SINGLETON pregnancies (4 426 691 naturally conceived, 78 300 fresh-ET and 18 037 frozen-ET singleton pregnancies; 33 209 sibships), and the claim's population field says only 'births' without that restriction.
